drafted_from: tool:list-clips-that-are-parts-of-a-series row in tool-rows.json, do-work/series_parts.py and test/test_series_parts.py
start_here: Say to your AI: "Find my clips that say they are part one, part two or part three of a series: read the moments files a.jsonl and b.jsonl and list them in order." It runs series_parts.py on your computer and shows the clips grouped by series.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads the moments files it is given and prints tab-separated lines and one result line.
instructions: 1. Have one or more moments files (JSON Lines, one row per spoken moment with id as <clip>#<n>, text, the clip's identity or name, path and source); cut your transcripts into moments first if you only have transcripts.

2. Say "Find my clips that are parts of a series" and name the moments files; your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs its command on your computer from the Workshop checkout, adding --out parts.tsv when the list is long.
3. Read the last line: {"result": {"clips", "series_parts", "within", "out"}} says how many clips were read and how many name a part; {"error": "what to change"} says what to fix.
4. Group the lines by series in part order to see which parts you have and which are missing; widen the window with --within 600 if a clip names its part late.

worked_examples.title: Three clips name a part and one does not
worked_examples.ask: Find my clips that are parts of a series in a.jsonl and b.jsonl.
worked_examples.given: From tools/list-clips-that-are-parts-of-a-series/test/test_series_parts.py: the command line is `python3 -I tools/list-clips-that-are-parts-of-a-series/do-work/series_parts.py a.jsonl b.jsonl`. a.jsonl holds six clips' moments (zeb#2 "and that is how the lantern got its glow.", zeb#1 "Okay this is part three of the lantern saga", alder#1 "Part 12. We open the copper box today.", mire#1 a walk by the pond, fennel#1 with "part two" after 300 characters, quell#1 "partly cloudy, the parts 5 arrived, the department 4 called"; clip paths /clips/<name>.mov, source cam-a). b.jsonl adds alder#2 "Then we close it." and loose#1 "PART ONE: the beginning" with source_file /other/loose.mp4.
worked_examples.hands_back: Three tab-separated lines ordered by path: "alder.mov, /clips/alder.mov, cam-a, part 12, Part 12. We open the copper box today. Then we close it."; "zeb.mov, /clips/zeb.mov, cam-a, part three, Okay this is part three of the lantern saga and that is how the lantern got its glow."; "loose.mp4, /other/loose.mp4, (empty source), part ONE, PART ONE: the beginning". Last line: {"result": {"clips": 6, "series_parts": 3, "within": 300, "out": null}}. fennel, mire and quell are not listed.
